reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code review confirms Phase 03's claim: validateDataColumnSidecar (gossip_validation.nim:586-716) lacks epoch-specific max_blobs_per_block validation. The verify_data_column_sidecar helper (peerdas_helpers.nim:352-366) only checks kzg_commitments.len > 0 and array length consistency, not the upper bound. In contrast, validateBeaconBlock calls validateBeaconBlockDeneb (line 857) which enforces blob_params.MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK check (lines 386-388). The 01e property (file: 01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json, lines 227-243) explicitly requires 'kzg_commitments count must not exceed max_blobs_per_block for the sidecar's epoch' per the assertion 'forall sidecar: len(sidecar.kzg_commitments) <= get_blob_parameters(epoch).max_blobs_per_block'. This is a real spec deviation. However, exploitability is constrained: (1) Attacker must be a selected proposer (validator role), limiting opportunity to their assigned slots. (2) The attack vector is semi-trusted boundary: proposer signs the sidecar's block header (verified at lines 689-696), making this a compromised validator scenario rather than arbitrary external attacker. (3) The inclusion proof validation (lines 629-632) ensures kzg_commitments consistency with body_root, so the eventual block with excessive commitments would be rejected by validateBeaconBlock when it arrives. (4) Impact is resource exhaustion (bandwidth, storage, CPU for KZG proofs on oversized sidecars) rather than consensus break or finalization disruption. (5) Attack scope is per-slot (one malicious sidecar set per proposer slot). Severity calibrated to Low per bug bounty scope: this is a validator misbehavior DoS vector with limited network-wide impact (<0.01% threshold), not a consensus vulnerability. Downgraded from High to Low due to semi-trusted boundary classification (requires validator compromise) and bounded impact (resource consumption, not safety violation).
